audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagreed. Content read Akali 1-6 then Azir at 2+ items; full read Skill on every row except Level 6.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer, and at 55.92% over 819 games Akali clearly owns the lane phase. Azir's late scaling and Emperor's Divide peel genuinely flip the last row, which both layers already agreed on in prose.
audit.corrected: Six full-layer rows flipped onto the content/packet chart as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] described Azir's 6 as 'a shuffle-into-ult combo' and never said what Emperor's Divide actually does to Akali.
audit.why: Emperor's Divide is a 120s wall of soldiers that knocks back and is flagged terrain. Terrain is the one thing that hard-stops both of Akali's dashes, so his level 6 is not a skirmish combo — it is the button that cancels her engage.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] rewritten around the 120s wall stopping E and R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shifting Sands appeared only as 'his shield-dash to a soldier'. The page never said the shield eats Akali's burst window, which is the interaction that decides every all-in. spikes[2] instead worried about him kiting with 'Arise! resets', which is not a mobility tool.
audit.why: Enemy E text: 'Azir shields himself briefly and dashes to one of his Sand Soldiers'. missingInteractions flagged shield-absorbs-burst. Arise! is a 1.5s soldier summon that replaces his basic attack in the soldier's range — it grants no movement.
audit.corrected: spikes[2], breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and wants.foe[1] now state that the shield absorbs the opening and must be forced out first.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's only defect reads: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere — needs concrete wait-for-X-before-you-Y lines', and sequencingCues was 0.
audit.why: Conquering Sands is 14s at rank 1 and costs up to 110 mana, Shifting Sands 22s, Emperor's Divide 120s. Those three numbers are the entire sequencing scheme of the matchup and none of them were on the page.
audit.corrected: All three written in, with explicit ordering: force the dash, then flip in during the gap; never commit into a held ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading advice never accounted for how Azir's damage is delivered.
audit.why: Sand Soldiers attack nearby targets for him and replace his basic attack only within the soldier's range. Twilight Shroud makes Akali unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks, which takes the soldiers' target away.
audit.corrected: whys[2] and breakdown.feeding now key the trade pattern to shrouding the soldier volley rather than to 'gaps in his wall'.

edits.before: Your pressure on his lack of soldiers and mana wins the early trades cleanly
edits.after: Conquering Sands is 14s at rank 1 — whiff it and he has no answer for 14 seconds

edits.before: Your dive can slip through his incomplete soldier wall and land cleanly
edits.after: Shroud takes the target away from his soldiers and his whole poke pattern stalls

edits.before: Your engage continues to outpace his positioning before his kit is fully set up
edits.after: Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1; once he burns it he cannot leave your E range

edits.before: Azir needs soldiers and levels to set up his zone control, so early trades favor you if you punish him before his wall of blades comes online.
edits.after: Conquering Sands costs up to 110 mana on a 14s cooldown at rank 1, so once he sends the soldiers through the wave, step up and take the trade before it comes back.

edits.before: Azir 6 gives him a shuffle-into-ult combo for skirmishes, but he's still fundamentally reliant on soldier positioning you can disrupt.
edits.after: Azir 6 adds Emperor's Divide, a 120s knockback wall that is real terrain — it stops your E dash and your R cold, so never commit into a held ultimate.

edits.before: Your burst item lets you close the gap through his soldier wall and delete him before he can kite with Arise! resets.
edits.after: Your burst item deletes him in one rotation, but Shifting Sands shields the opening — force the dash out first, then flip in on the 22s gap.

edits.before: Azir is weak and passive before he has soldiers stacked and mana to spend, so you can punish his approach and farming pattern directly, using your mobility to bypass his early poke attempts.
edits.after: Azir stays passive until his mana affords Conquering Sands every 14s, and his soldiers only replace his auto inside their own range — walk him off the wave and Q his toes each time a soldier expires.

edits.before: You continue to dominate through his 6 — his soldier wall takes time and resources to set up, and your Shroud-E dive can slip through the gaps before he fully establishes zone control, keeping this comfortably in your favor.
edits.after: You continue to dominate through his 6 — Shifting Sands is 22s and Emperor's Divide 120s, so he owns two answers and both are slow. Bait the dash, shroud the soldiers off you, and flip in while both are counting down.

edits.before: Flip in through gaps in his soldier wall before he can reposition
edits.after: Force out Shifting Sands, then flip in during its 22-second gap

edits.before: Use Arise! resets and shuffle to zone your engage in skirmishes
edits.after: Shield-dash away with Shifting Sands the moment you commit

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Twilight Shroud for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Shifting Sands: 22s at rank 1, and it shields him as it dashes — force it out before you commit or your burst hits the shield. - Emperor's Divide (120s) is real terrain and stops your E dash and R. - Conquering Sands is 14s at rank 1.

edits.before: Track Azir’s Shifting Sands: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Shifting Sands (22s) shields him mid-dash, so bait it out before you burst. Emperor's Divide is terrain — his wall stops your E dash and your R.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — one carry per fight, every fight; the shroud buys the time and the resets pay the exit.
edits.after: Carry by opening in the 22s after Shifting Sands: without the shield-dash Azir cannot leave your E range.

edits.before: If Azir opens the score, reset expectations and respect Shifting Sands doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q range and stay relevant through shroud picks.
edits.after: If Azir opens the score his soldiers hold you off the whole wave — farm at Q range, shroud the soldier volleys off you, and step up only in the window Shifting Sands is counting down.

notes: The claim that Twilight Shroud denies Azir's Sand Soldiers a target is derived from two Riot descriptions (soldiers 'attack nearby targets for him'; the shroud makes Akali 'unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks') rather than from a documented interaction, so I marked that audit point Medium and kept the wording to what the two texts jointly support.
